peer keeps working against a newer one. The helper drops one before it reaches the main actor,
so it costs the device’s input nothing. A new kind that would arrive often, as the frame
acknowledgement does, is sent only to a peer that said it takes it. The kind numbers the
upstream protocol used for features Headwire does not take stay unused, so a capture of either
protocol never reads as the other, and so do the numbers Headwire retired, which released
helpers may still act on. The generation is raised only for a change an older peer cannot skip;
the new generation then gets a session application protocol of its own beside the current one.

builds the TLS options for both ends. Each side presents a self-signed P-256
certificate (

SubjectPublicKeyInfo (

are never evaluated. Session tickets and resumption are off, so a removed device can’t return on
an old ticket.
